_meta.note: verbatim fields contain exact captured output. commentary fields contain human interpretation.

wrapperFormat.commentary: This is the wrapper structure observed around each tool result as rendered into this agent's context (bracket-notation used here in place of literal angle brackets per capture convention). It was consistent across view, glob, create, edit, powershell, sql, and fetch_copilot_cli_documentation calls. One exception was observed: a single grep 'content' mode success result appeared as bare unwrapped text rather than inside this wrapper (see tools.grep.cases.success_with_matches_content_mode below) — this may indicate an inconsistency in how single-line/plain-text grep results are surfaced versus other tools, but was not exhaustively reproduced across many trials.

large_file_default_params.verbatim: File too large to read at once (108.4 KB). Consider using the grep tool to search within the file, or view with view_range to read specific sections.
large_file_default_params.commentary: Contrary to a generic 'read tool with default line limit' expectation, this harness's view tool does NOT return a truncated default-length excerpt for large files. It outright refuses and returns only this short advisory message with zero file content, unless the caller supplies view_range or forceReadLargeFiles:true. Confirmed threshold description: >20KB (matches the tool's documented '20KB' truncation limit in its own schema description).

with_matches.commentary: Results returned as Windows backslash paths prefixed with '.\', regardless of the forward-slash pattern supplied. Order was NOT alphabetical (varied-content-test.txt listed before large-file-3000-lines.txt) — order appears to be filesystem/OS enumeration order, not lexicographic.

no_matches.commentary: Plain sentence, no error status, no empty-list/array representation.

success_with_matches_content_mode.commentary: Format is '{path}:{full matching line text}' (ripgrep-style), one line per match. Notably, THIS particular call's result rendered WITHOUT the [result][name][output] wrapper seen for other tool calls in this session — appeared as bare text. Not fully explained; flagged as an open question about wrapper consistency.

no_matches.commentary: Plain sentence, consistent phrasing style with glob's no-match message.

with_glob_filter_count_mode.commentary: Only files WITH at least one match are listed in count mode ('{path}:{count}'); files with zero matches (varied-content-test.txt did not contain 'hotel') are silently omitted rather than shown with a 0. Path mixes forward slashes (from the supplied paths root) and a backslash before the filename.

denied_by_repo_hook_with_line_numbers_fl.verbatim: Denied by preToolUse hook from "repo settings" (hook errored)
denied_by_repo_hook_with_line_numbers_fl.commentary: Reproduced twice with identical parameters — not a flake. This is workspace/repo-specific: a preToolUse hook configured in this repository's settings intercepts grep calls that request line numbers (-n: true) and denies them, and the denial message itself states the hook 'errored' during evaluation, suggesting a fail-closed default on hook error rather than an explicit deny rule. The identical call WITHOUT -n:true succeeded normally. This is a repo/session-specific finding, not necessarily a general GHCP CLI harness default — flagged as environment-specific and may not reproduce in other repos/workspaces.

error_nonzero_exit.call: powershell({command: "Write-Error \"deliberate test error\"; exit 7", description: "Simple failing command for output capture"})
error_nonzero_exit.verbatim:
try { [Console]::OutputEncoding = [System.Text.UTF8Encoding]::new($false) } catch {}; try { if (Get-Variable -Name PSStyle -ErrorAction Ignore) { $PSStyle.OutputRendering = 'PlainText' } } catch {}; $global:LASTEXITCODE = 0; $__copilotCommandFinished = $false; $__copilotSuccess = $false; try { $global:LASTEXITCODE = 0
Write-Error "deliberate test error"; exit 7
$__copilotSuccess = $?
$__copilotCommandFinished = $true
 } finally { if ($__copilotCommandFinished) { if (-not $__copilotSuccess -and $LASTEXITCODE -is [int] -and $LASTEXITCODE -ne 0) { $host.SetShouldExit($LASTEXITCODE) } elseif (-not $__copilotSuccess) { $host.SetShouldExit(1) } else { $host.SetShouldExit(0) } } } : deliberate test error
    + CategoryInfo          : NotSpecified: (:) [Write-Error], WriteErrorException
    + FullyQualifiedErrorId : Microsoft.PowerShell.Commands.WriteErrorException
[shellId: 38 completed with exit code 7]
error_nonzero_exit.commentary: Reveals the harness's internal PowerShell wrapper: sets UTF8 console encoding, disables PSStyle ANSI rendering, tracks success/exit-code in wrapper variables, and calls $host.SetShouldExit(...) in a finally block to propagate exit codes. The user's literal command is spliced verbatim into the middle of this wrapper script, and appears (confusingly, since it's an artifact of PowerShell echoing the failing statement in the error record) inline with the error text. Final status line correctly reports exit code 7.

long_output_saved_to_temp_file.commentary: Unlike 'view' (which refuses outright for oversized files), 'powershell' with oversized output writes the FULL output to an OS temp file (revealing an absolute path under the invoking user's AppData\Local\Temp) and returns only a short preview (first 500 chars) plus follow-up tool suggestions (grep, head/tail, view with view_range, jq). Threshold appears to be similar in magnitude to view's 20KB (here 23.3KB triggered it).
